q: How do I make Revolution keep a copy of my server footage on this computer?
a: Settings ▸ Media Cache ▸ Network Copies ▸ Local copies of clips on network shares (`mediaCache.networkCopies`). It's Automatic by default: Revolution copies each clip whose file is on a network share into the media cache folder (`Network Copies`), in the background, and once a copy is complete it reads the copy instead of the share. The clip's badge in the Project panel changes from NET to NET ✓.

q: Is the local copy of a network clip re-encoded or compressed?
a: No. It is byte-for-byte the same file, so the picture, the grade and exports are exactly as from the original. That's the difference from proxies or optimized media, which are re-encoded smaller files.

q: How do I change how much space network copies may take?
a: Settings ▸ Media Cache ▸ Network Copies ▸ Local copies size limit (`mediaCache.networkCopiesGb`, 100 GB by default). Above it the copies used least recently are deleted, the open project's last. Revolution only ever deletes copies it made.

q: How do I stop Revolution from copying files off my server?
a: Set Settings ▸ Media Cache ▸ Network Copies ▸ Local copies of clips on network shares (`mediaCache.networkCopies`) to Off. Then it never reads or makes copies and plays every clip from the share itself.

q: Where on disk do the network copies go?
a: Into the media cache folder, in a folder called Network Copies. The Media Cache management policy leaves that folder alone; the copies are managed only by the Local copies size limit (`mediaCache.networkCopiesGb`).

q: The copy paused when I hit play. Is something wrong?
a: No, that's on purpose: copies are made in the background, one file at a time, only while you aren't playing, so they never compete with playback. The copy carries on from where it stopped a few seconds after you stop.

q: How will I know a clip has finished copying to this computer?
a: A message says Local copy of A001.mov ready: it now plays from this computer, and in the Project panel the clip's badge changes from NET to NET ✓; hovering it adds …; plays from its local copy.

q: What if a file is changed on the server while it's being copied?
a: That copy isn't kept; the file is copied again later. A copy always belongs to one version of the file, so a changed file never plays from an out-of-date copy.

q: What happens to a half-finished copy when the share drops?
a: The copy fails and says so (the share dropped, or the disk is full), its half-made file is removed, and that file isn't tried again until Revolution restarts. Clips with a complete copy keep playing from it.

q: Do network copies change how my export looks?
a: No. The copy is byte-for-byte the original file, so the picture, the grade and exports are exactly the same as from the share.

q: My NAS goes to sleep every night; how do I set up so I can still edit late?
a: Leave Settings ▸ Media Cache ▸ Network Copies ▸ Local copies of clips on network shares (`mediaCache.networkCopies`) on Automatic and give the copies time to finish while the NAS is awake (each clip shows NET ✓ when its copy is done). When the share stops answering, Revolution uses the last complete copies, so those clips keep working. A clip without a copy goes offline after 8 seconds instead of freezing the app, and comes back online by itself when the NAS wakes; nothing needs relinking.

q: How is that different from making proxies?
a: Network copies are the original files copied byte for byte, so nothing is re-encoded and the picture, grade and exports are identical. Proxies are smaller re-encoded files. Resolve and Premiere expect proxies or optimized media for slow storage; in Revolution proxies still work as before and are the better choice when the local disk is small, while copies need room for the full camera files (100 GB limit by default, `mediaCache.networkCopiesGb`).

q: ok and what if I don't want it using my disk at all
a: Set Settings ▸ Media Cache ▸ Network Copies ▸ Local copies of clips on network shares (`mediaCache.networkCopies`) to Off: nothing is copied and clips always play from the share. If you only want less space used, lower Local copies size limit (`mediaCache.networkCopiesGb`) instead.

context.q: why is filmcraft copying my nas files?
context.a: It keeps local copies of clips on network shares (Automatic by default) so they play smoothly and keep working if the share drops; a clip shows NET ✓ when its copy is complete.
